issues.description: The solution repository's client-side PersonScene.java (solution_repository/src/client/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/view/PersonScene.java) introduces an import and a final field of the server-side type PersonService (de.tum.in.ase.eist.service.PersonService). This both (a) violates the layered architecture described in the problem statement (client should interact with the server via the Network/Application layers and via PersonController, not by referencing server-side service classes directly) and (b) leaves a final field (personService) uninitialized in the PersonScene class, which will cause a compilation error. The template version of PersonScene does not declare or import PersonService and relies solely on PersonController, which matches the problem statement. Having the solution introduce a server-side dependency into client UI code is an unintentional structural inconsistency that will confuse students and prevent using the solution as a correct reference.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the import and the final PersonService field from the client-side PersonScene in the solution. The client view should interact only with the PersonController (as in the template) and not reference server-side service classes. If server-side functionality is needed, use the existing controller + WebClient flow. Also ensure any fields declared as final are properly initialized in the constructor (or not final) so the code compiles.
